premises.text: Mobile-device users still rely on outlets and plug-in chargers for everyday battery power
premises.evidence_span: scurrying around trying to find an outlet just to get a little bit more juice in your phone

premises.text: A proprietary RF-harvesting smartphone case captures wasted phone RF energy, converts it to electricity, and extends battery life without plugging in
premises.evidence_span: Our case is embedded with a harvesting antenna that is proprietary that captures that wasted RF energy and then takes it through a conversion process to convert it into electricity and then dumps it back into the phone

premises.text: A large share of US smartphone users already buy products to get more phone power
premises.evidence_span: out of the 220 million smartphone users in the United States, over 30% have purchased some sort of product to help them get a little more power in their phone

premises.text: The case launches via Kickstarter as the go-to-market channel
premises.evidence_span: in one month, we are launching this product. And we will be doing that on Kickstarter

premises.text: A follow-on wireless charger will provide near- and far-field powering where consumers are
premises.evidence_span: Our next product that we're going to bring to the market is a wireless charger that will provide near field and far field powering solutions

domains.name: RF harvesting case and wireless roadmap

value.text: Consumers get passive extra phone battery life from wasted RF without hunting for outlets
value.evidence_span: it gives you extra power that you need to get from sunup to sundown

secondary_value.text: Green harvesting of wasted energy instead of plug-in battery packs
secondary_value.evidence_span: It is a green technology that simply harvests wasted energy and converts it into DC power

causal_links.evidence_span: you as a consumer deserve a better solution for power for your mobile devices
extend your battery life by 30% simply using wasted energy transmitted from your phone
over 30% have purchased some sort of product to help them get a little more power in their phone

notes: Outlet-hunting and plug-in charger dependence folded as one pain (§4.1.6). Antenna/conversion/dump-back/30%/unplugged vs battery cases folded as one RF-harvest case mechanism (§4.1.7). IoT ambient-sensor uses treated as applications of the same RF harvesting (§4.1.2). Ubiquitous wireless-power dream treated as vision framing; concrete next wireless-charger product retained. OSU inventors treated as credentials. Singleton D1 retained as separately revisable problem premise. Anti-template: problem, product roadmap, and market/GTM separately revisable.
